definitions.explanation: A large ocean fish of the family Scombridae, highly prized in Japanese cuisine for sushi and sashimi. Various species and cuts exist at different price points.

examples.japanese: マグロ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。

examples.english: I watched the tuna auction at Tsukiji.

examples.japanese: ⟦{回転寿司|かいてんずし}→回転寿司：11900_kaitenzushi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧マグロ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ネタ→ネタ：06309_neta⟧だ。
examples.english: Tuna is the most popular topping at conveyor belt sushi.

notes:
USAGE:
The most popular sushi and sashimi fish in Japan. Different cuts and species have distinct names and price ranges.

COMMON CUTS:
- ⟦{赤身|あかみ}→赤身：19617_akami⟧ (lean red meat — most affordable)
- {中|ちゅう}トロ (medium-fatty tuna)
- {大|おお}トロ (fatty tuna belly — most expensive)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マグロ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{刺身|さしみ}→刺身：04023_sashimi⟧ (tuna sashimi)
- マグロ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{握|にぎ}り (tuna nigiri sushi)
- マグロ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{漬|づ}け (marinated tuna)
- マグロ{丼|どん} (tuna rice bowl)
- {本|ほん}マグロ (bluefin tuna — the most prized variety)

WRITING:
Usually written in katakana (マグロ) in menus and everyday use. The kanji {鮪|まぐろ} exists but is less common outside formal or literary contexts.
